skill.name: set-up-shopify-google-ads-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up and verify Shopify repeat-order conversions in Google Ads. Choose revenue or profit as the bidding value for a retention campaign.
skill.summary: Set up and verify Shopify repeat-order bidding in Google Ads with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static flags are Markdown formatting, public links, or ordinary checks of connected accounts. The unpinned installer and remote MCP fallback present real execution and trust risks. The review also found gaps in setup approval, credential handling, order data minimization, and live documentation verification.

remediation.issue: The install example can run an unpinned package and install an unpinned skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and skill commit. Document the publisher and require separate user approval before any installation.

remediation.issue: The workflow can fall back to a remote MCP endpoint without a separate trust decision.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval for an authenticated MCP connection. Show the endpoint, workspace, and permissions before sending account identifiers or making calls.

remediation.issue: Prerequisite setup can change tracking or extend it beyond Google Ads.
remediation.suggestion: Limit setup to the selected Shopify store and Google Ads account. Ask before each material write or new data destination. Keep consent changes user-controlled.

remediation.issue: The skill allows unrelated platform credentials to pass through the assistant and CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Remove those exceptions from this skill. Direct users to verified platform authorization screens or a secure credential input that bypasses chat and command arguments.

remediation.issue: Order lookup guidance does not limit retrieved data to what the check needs.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the storefront before fetching orders. Set a small result limit and request only classification and required value fields. Report aggregates when possible.

remediation.issue: Live documentation can replace the reviewed local workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle versioned reference files. Treat any live documentation as untrusted and do not let it add tools, destinations, permissions, or account changes.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopify Returning Customer Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A general purchase goal does not distinguish repeat orders from first orders. This skill helps you verify repeat-order tracking and choose a revenue or profit goal for a Google Ads retention campaign.
actual_capabilities: Checks Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP and identifies missing Shopify or Google Ads setup steps.
Checks whether recent Shopify orders count as new, returning, or unknown.
Guides setup of secondary conversion actions for returning customer revenue and profit.
Explains how to set a campaign-specific goal and choose a target return on ad spend.
Guides a repeat-order test and verifies the selected conversion action status after a manual Google Ads change.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics and active server-side tracking between Shopify and Google Ads. The setup guide also requires a linked Merchant Center account.
A user must approve Shopify and Google access and change the primary conversion goal in Google Ads.
Profit conversions require complete costs and active additional cost settings. Orders without usable customer history may remain unclassified.
Does not set up new-customer or lifetime value bidding. It does not guarantee returns or conversion volume.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Shopify store for repeat-order tracking
use_cases.description: Check whether your store and Google Ads account are connected. Identify which setup steps require your approval.

use_cases.title: Choose a goal for a retention campaign
use_cases.description: Compare repeat-order revenue and profit goals. Plan a campaign-specific change without changing acquisition campaigns.

use_cases.title: Validate a repeat-order conversion
use_cases.description: Check whether a test order counts as returning. Verify that the selected conversion action has the expected status in Google Ads.

prompt_templates.title: Check setup readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my Shopify store and Google Ads account are ready for returning customer bidding. List missing prerequisites without changing any settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: You need a setup checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Review order classifications
prompt_templates.prompt: After I confirm the storefront, summarize how many of its last 20 Shopify orders are new, returning, or unknown. Do not include customer identifiers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Tracking is connected and you want to verify classifications.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a campaign-specific goal
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare repeat-order revenue and profit for my retention campaign. Show the manual Google Ads steps for the recommended goal, and leave other campaigns unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: You are choosing what your retention campaign should value.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a profit bidding rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my test order classification, cost readiness, current conversion goal, and target ROAS. Flag any mismatch and list the manual checks still needed. Do not make changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: You are validating a profit-based campaign setup.

output_examples.input: Check whether I can start setting up returning customer bidding.
output: Shopify is connected to Product Metrics.
Google Ads setup is incomplete. Link the client account and confirm its Merchant Center connection before creating conversion actions.

output_examples.input: Which goal should my retention campaign use if some product costs are missing?
output: Start with Product Metrics - Returning Customer. This action values repeat-order revenue.
Wait to use Product Metrics - Returning Customer Profit until your costs are complete.
Set a campaign-specific goal so other campaigns keep their existing goals.

output_examples.input: Check the repeat-order test and tell me what to do next.
output: The paid test order is classified as returning.
The returning customer revenue action exists and is still secondary.
Review your retention campaign in Google Ads before changing its conversion goal.

best_practices: Confirm the Shopify storefront, Google Ads client account, and consent settings before enabling tracking.
Verify a paid repeat order in your payment provider's test mode before changing a campaign goal.
Start with one retention campaign and use a campaign-specific goal to preserve other campaign settings.
anti_patterns: Making multiple purchase actions primary for the same campaign goal.
Choosing the profit action before the required cost data is complete.
Pasting credentials or identifiable order details into the assistant conversation.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. Product Metrics processes Shopify orders and sends conversion events to the connected Google Ads account.

faq.question: What counts as a returning customer?
faq.answer: Product Metrics checks for an earlier order tied to the same Shopify customer. An order from before app installation can count.

faq.question: Does every paid repeat order count?
faq.answer: Yes, when Shopify identifies the customer as returning and consent requirements are met. The conversion is per eligible order, not per customer.

faq.question: Which action should I use for profit bidding?
faq.answer: Choose Product Metrics - Returning Customer Profit if your product costs are complete and your additional costs are active.

faq.question: Can the assistant make my goal primary?
faq.answer: No. The guide leaves that decision and change to you in Google Ads. The assistant can explain the steps and check the resulting status.

faq.question: Will other campaigns need the same goal?
faq.answer: No. Use a campaign-specific goal for the retention campaign to keep other campaigns on their existing goals.
